The unchanged exact decode DAG has one recurrent chain per request.
Already-ready requests or prefill chunks can supply additional work.
Their existence does not make later recurrent states of one token available.
See [the frontier contract](../reports/exact_frontier_contract.md).

NanoFlow already batches independent operator work and reuses physical weight pointers.
MPK already supplies persistent task workers and device-side control.
These are stronger generic controls than a host-launched eager baseline.
See [the ownership audit](../reports/operator_ownership_nearest_audit.md) and [the persistent audit](../reports/persistent_execution_redteam.md).

The P2/P4 component lane measures an ideal already-ready supply.
It does not execute a complete legal distributed request.
At P2, Base1.4B, one row, stream medians are 0.03707 ms local, 0.02994 ms TP, and 0.06178 ms remote round-trip.
These are warm same-operator measurements.
They are not full-stack weight-residency measurements.

Current status: `GENERIC_ONLY` for ordinary ready-task pooling.
A genuinely new ownership mechanism remains unestablished.
Reopen only with a concrete ready-work pattern and an incremental benefit over aliased generic batching.

## Evidence update 1

The measured one-owner/one-worker layout keeps attention and its historical KV on the source.
It sends a complete post-attention MLP input to a remote full-weight worker.
The source waits for the complete returned output before its following normalization and layer.

| State | Owner and lifetime | Required transfer |
|---|---|---|
| Historical depth/layer KV | Attention owner, committed request prefix | None for this layout |
| Current attention state and residual | Attention owner, current exact version | None for this layout |
| MLP weights | Remote worker, immutable checkpoint | Resident before the test |
| MLP input | Source, after required normalization | 4096 bytes per BF16 row |
| MLP output | Worker, after down projection | 4096 bytes per BF16 row |

The P2/P4 graph-captured test includes both directions and the complete dense MLP.
The returned source output matches the local component bitwise on the tested inputs.
The remote path is slower at every tested row count for both checkpoints.
This prunes that layout for an isolated request with unchanged serial attention work.
It does not reject every pooled or hybrid A/FFN architecture.

KernelFlume and AFD are direct generic ownership controls.
The useful pooled frontier and the strongest same-P baseline remain necessary for a different layout.
Current status: `NO_NET_HEADROOM` in the tested one-owner layout, with `GENERIC_ONLY` novelty as presently defined.

The symbolic address protocol passes 729 small exit histories.
It compares 93312 logical K/V values with explicit terminal copying.
The GPU interface probe also passes distinct-depth page-table reads at page sizes 16 and 1.
It checks unique private current-row appends for a four-row fixture.
These tests do not implement a compact allocator or a live alias runtime.
They do not establish model-output parity.

The immutable mapping uses the computed depth `min(requested_depth, terminal_depth)` for a completed adaptive token.
Fixed R4 retains four distinct computed states.
Removing adaptive terminal copies therefore supplies no fixed-R4 copy-saving claim.

Enabling Dynamic Computation already describes original-gate Ragged KV with the same terminal-depth value rule.
WaveFront already implements per-row depth indexing.
The standalone address mechanism is a direct prior overlap, not a new distributed axis.
See [the runtime boundary audit](../reports/dynamic_runtime_prior_boundary.md).

Current status: `GENERIC_ONLY` as an architecture claim.
No-copy terminal publication is `MODE_SPECIFIC` and already has a direct prior.
The remaining question concerns a distinct distributed ownership design, not another alias-only implementation.

The changed assumption is provisional correction, not authoritative stale-state replacement.
Only a causal embedding or one exact current-token pass initializes the guesses.
The numerical probe evaluates actual pretrained full cores with the correct depth-indexed history.
It overwrites private current-token rows, never future-token history.
Reference future states enter diagnostics only.

Both Base sizes run two single-token probes, one per task domain.
Jacobi and identity-surrogate correction recover the exact boundary trace after four zero-warm-up rounds.
With one exact warm-up pass, three correction rounds recover it.
Current-token KV also matches at those recovery points.
Earlier token agreement can coexist with large internal KV error.

Four ideal core rounds do not beat four sequential core passes before added costs.
The actual numerical executor is serial on one GPU.
It measures no four-way solver speedup or free-running candidate quality.
See `outputs/finite_correction_base14_v1/` and `outputs/finite_correction_base26_v1/`.

Jacobi finite-chain correction, surrogate correction, and KV repair have direct prior art.
See [the parallel sampler audit](../reports/parallel_sampling_nearest_audit.md).
Current status: `NO_NET_HEADROOM` for the tested exact-recovery schedule.
Finite-round approximation remains `QUALITY_UNRESOLVED`, not a qualifying new architecture.

## Evidence update 1

The exact real-arithmetic identity requires both `W*base` and the fresh dense `W*delta`.
The second multiplication does not become cheap because delta has a small norm.
Normalization needs a fresh denominator.
SwiGLU and attention softmax cannot generally reuse separately transformed additive components.

The CPU audit includes valid algebra and BF16 counterexamples.
It proves no model-quality property.
The captured BF16 inputs also show few bitwise-equal elements between tested recurrent versions.
This observation does not prove every possible residual representation is dense.
It supplies no exact sparse-compute guarantee.

Current status: `NO_NET_HEADROOM` for the unchanged dense base-plus-delta formula.
A lower-cost representation needs independent evidence and matched free-running quality.
No approximate distributed implementation runs in this campaign checkpoint.

## Evidence update 1

The CPU screen inspects 108 bounded activation pairs per checkpoint.
It reconstructs original BF16 bits exactly through XOR and a reversible byte layout.
Observed size ratios are not GPU codec timings.
Fixed-decode XOR/byte-plane/zlib ratios are approximately 0.779 and 0.771 of the original bytes for the two models.
Raw zlib alone is approximately 0.809 for both.
The observation is a limited input sample, not a universal entropy bound.

The P2 physical probe measures transport startup and an unfused reversible transform separately.
The transform excludes entropy encoding, decoding, metadata, and receiver-base management.
Its overhead is already comparable to a small-message broadcast in this tested path.
No executable compressed serving path or E2E gain is established.

Current status: `NO_NET_HEADROOM` for the tested unfused small-message premise.
A fused codec remains untested and faces generic lossless-transport prior art.
The representation does not expose independent future recurrent work.
